handoff.purpose: Generate deterministic mutants over real functions with documented no-go filters, rejections, and inspectable counters.

symbols.name: OPERATORS
symbols.note: Tuple of five mutation operators: DROP_CALL, INVERT_CONDITION, WEAKEN_COMPARISON, CHANGE_CONSTANT, DROP_ARGUMENT, EARLY_RETURN.

symbols.name: OPERATOR_CLASS
symbols.note: Maps each operator to a defect class string for comparison with the hand corpus.

symbols.name: generate
symbols.note: Deterministic mutant generator over real functions; reads source files, parses ASTs, samples sites, applies operators, and returns a list of Mutant objects.

claims.text: Generate ``count`` parseable mutants over real functions. Deterministic.
claims.why: The function uses random.Random(seed) for all randomness, and the seed defaults to 20260730; the same seed and inputs will produce the same sequence of choices, so generation is deterministic. The output is a list of Mutant objects whose 'after' field has been validated by ast.parse, so the mutants are parseable.

claims.text: a big file cannot dominate merely by being walked first
claims.why: Sites are collected across all files first, then rng.shuffle(sites) is applied, so the order of files in the walk does not bias the sampling.

claims.text: the filters were defined, documented as built, and CALLED FROM NOWHERE
claims.why: The comment names SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block, and covered_lines, and states they each appeared exactly once in this file (their own definition). In this chunk, _in_main_block is called at line 338, and SKIP_PATH_PARTS and SKIP_FUNCTIONS are used at lines 324 and 333, so the claim that they were 'CALLED FROM NOWHERE' is a historical claim about an earlier state; the comment itself describes that past state, and the code now calls them. The claim is about what was measured on 2026-07-30, and the comment accurately reports that measurement; the current code contradicts the historical state, but the claim is kept as a factual report of the past.

claims.text: a filter whose effect nobody can observe is one refactor away from being a filter nobody calls
claims.why: The code publishes generate.last_filtered and generate.last_rejected, so the effects of the filters are observable; the comment's reasoning is consistent with the code's behavior.

claims.text: a syntax error is a typo, not a defect
claims.why: The code catches SyntaxError from ast.parse(mutated) and continues, treating a syntax error as a reason to skip, consistent with the comment's claim.

claims.text: Undetectable by construction. Keeping it would depress every score measured against this corpus for a reason that is not the detector's fault, which is exactly how a metric starts lying.
claims.why: The code checks trivially_equivalent(original, mutated) and skips the mutant, recording it in rejected['trivially_equivalent']. This matches the comment's rationale.
generate.last_rejected is set to a sorted dict, making the rejection counts inspectable.

claims.text: Sites the no-go filters refused BEFORE a mutation was ever attempted. Published for the same reason as ``last_rejected``: a filter whose effect nobody can observe is one refactor away from being a filter nobody calls, which is exactly the state these were found in.
claims.why: generate.last_filtered is set to a sorted dict of refusal reasons, and the code records refusals via _refuse before any mutation attempt, matching the comment.

observations.what: The comment at lines 315-318 explicitly states that SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block, and covered_lines were previously defined but never called. In this chunk, _in_main_block is called at line 338, and SKIP_PATH_PARTS and SKIP_FUNCTIONS are used at lines 324 and 333, but _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, and covered_lines are not called in this chunk. The comment's historical claim is accurate for the measured date; the current code has partially fixed the issue.
The function generate reads files from the include directory using rglob, which is a filesystem read. It does not write to the filesystem, spawn processes, make network requests, or spend money.

The code uses ast.unparse to produce the 'before' and 'after' fields of Mutant objects. ast.unparse may not preserve the original source formatting exactly, which could affect the fidelity of the mutants, but this is not a defect in the chunk's claims.
The function returns an empty list if no files are found (line 289) or if no sites are collected, which is a valid edge case.
